channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Accelerating LLM Pretraining with Zeroth-Order Curvature on Idle Serving Compute
item.description: ZO-Curv replaces the standard AdamW pretraining update with a curvature-adapted first-order update, where curvature is estimated by forward-only zeroth-order queries dispatched to idle inference-serving hardware that would otherwise sit unused. The cost is a heterogeneous training-and-serving orchestration layer, finite-query curvature estimation noise, and the need for serving devices that can run the model's forward pass while a separate training node performs first-order steps. The approach can fail when insufficient idle serving compute is available, when noisy curvature estimates mislead the update at small query budgets, or when the operational complexity of co-scheduling training and serving outweighs the wall-clock gain. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GraTED: Graph--Tensor EEG Decoding for Passenger Hazard Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
item.description: GraTED replaces 2D-grid CNN-style EEG classifiers with graph convolutions over electrode scalp geometry plus low-rank tensor classification of time-feature representations. The cost is a specialized preprocessing and modeling pipeline (electrode-graph construction, tensor decomposition) and a task-specific architecture rather than a general-purpose component. It can fail to generalize beyond the small 11-subject dataset, requires EEG hardware and AV hazard-label infrastructure the reader likely lacks, and offers no quantified accuracy margin over baselines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
item.description: KAN variants replace the tuned MLP as the classifier on structured clinical tabular data. They cost 1.20x-1.48x more inference latency and up to 12.5x more parameters, with no systematic pooled accuracy advantage. Gains are confined to severely imbalanced cohorts (minority-class AUPRC), so adoption on balanced data, or where latency and model size dominate, yields overhead without benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
item.description: TensorLOB replaces the standard flattening of limit order book state into matrices with end-to-end tensor operations: mode-wise contractions for feature extraction and direct contraction with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, preserving the time, side, level, and attribute structure. The cost is a specialized tensor implementation, training effort on a domain-specific pipeline, and no quantified efficiency gain; compute savings are not claimed. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on the small FI-2010 benchmark, so gains may not transfer to other instruments, exchanges, or live data with nonstationarity and latency constraints. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion at Test Time
item.description: Replaces personalization via multi-pose subject videos or real multi-frame capture with self-generated supervision: a pose-conditioned generator synthesizes pseudo-ground-truth frames, an inference-time sampler filters them for identity consistency, and a per-subject low-rank adapter trains on static clips of the survivors. Costs include extra test-time compute per subject (candidate generation, identity scoring, and a small LoRA training run) plus pipeline complexity, and synthetic frames are explicitly lower in fidelity than real ones. Failure modes include the pseudo-GT generator or identity filter propagating reference-image errors into the adapter, degraded results when the target pose departs far from anything the generator synthesizes well, and per-subject adaptation latency that may not fit interactive serving budgets. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SHq: Learnable Grids for LLM Weight Quantization
item.description: SHq replaces the fixed lookup-table grids (INT, FP, NF, BOF) in block-scaled LUT quantization formats such as NF4, BOF4, and NVFP4 with a closed-form grid parameterized by a companding strength and an offset, requiring only modification of table contents. It costs a per-format grid selection or fitting step and reuses the otherwise-unused sign bit of the FP8 block scale; it adds no runtime latency or memory overhead since it is a drop-in grid replacement. It can fail if downstream kernels or hardware LUT instructions hardcode specific grids, if the optimal parameters do not transfer across models or layers, or if gains measured in KL divergence do not hold for the reader's specific tasks at very low bit-widths. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
item.description: The method replaces an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server for long-context LLM serving with a Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster of pooled economical accelerators connected by fast interconnects. It requires specialized hardware with integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay, which imposes a high engineering and acquisition cost. The approach can fail if the interconnect is not sufficiently fast, as TCP-class communication reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding
item.description: Replaces purely semantic SID construction and likelihood-only beam scoring in generative recommendation with utility-enriched semantic codes and beam scores augmented by predicted post-exposure utility. Costs include maintaining per-item utility estimates with incremental updates and training multiple post-exposure outcome predictors, though SID length, vocabulary, and decoding cost are unchanged. Can fail if utility predictors are inaccurate or drift faster than incremental code updates, causing beam scoring to mis-rank candidates, and the reported gain presupposes an existing deployed generative recommendation pipeline at platform scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
item.description: The technique replaces per-topology sparse refactorization of the Jacobian with a single reference matrix inversion and low-rank Woodbury corrections for topology changes. It requires implementing a Newton--Raphson solver with inner iterative methods (truncated Neumann or BiCGStab) and storing the inverted reference matrix plus correction factors. The approach can fail if the spectral radius of the iteration matrix exceeds unity or if the condition number makes the reference Jacobian an ineffective preconditioner for specific outage scenarios. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches
item.description: Replaces per-vessel models and transfer or federated adaptation pipelines with a single LightGBM model trained on pooled fleet data, where each vessel is described by its identity and seven static specifications, using only inputs available before departure. Costs are modest: one model to train and maintain instead of many, no distributed infrastructure, and accuracy that does not improve further with per-vessel fine-tuning. It can fail for vessels whose specifications differ substantially from the training fleet, and its zero-shot advantage depends on specification coverage rather than on ship identity alone. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
item.description: DepthGraft replaces standard per-layer KV computation (and prior adjacent/global-anchor KV sharing) with a pretraining-time architecture where deep-layer KV is reconstructed from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. It costs a full pretraining run under a modified architecture, adds cross-layer reconstruction logic to the model definition, and yields only about one-third KV cache reduction at inference. It can fail because all results are pretraining-based on 0.5B-16B models, so the method cannot be retrofitted to existing checkpoints, the reported gains may not transfer to other data mixes or scales, and third-party implementations of an unverified arXiv architecture may diverge. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
item.description: PagedMoE replaces storing each bit-width of an SSD-resident MoE expert as an independent cache object with a single prefix-compatible tree-codebook and bitplane layout, so cached low-precision data is reused and only missing bitplanes are fetched for higher precision. It costs a custom storage format, direct execution on 1-8-bit prefixes, and offline per-expert error profiles to select prefix length before I/O. It can fail if the routing-weight-based precision selection misestimates importance on out-of-distribution inputs, and the reported gains are demonstrated only on very large MoE models that require SSD offloading, so benefits may vanish for models that already fit in DRAM. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
item.description: ARCBench replaces ad hoc or out-of-harness checks of rule compliance after context compaction with an action-level benchmark on the open-source pi agent harness, measuring whether agents actually obey operating rules during execution. It costs engineering effort to instrument the harness, define rules, and run evaluation episodes, plus API or GPU inference for each configuration; it is an evaluation tool, not a production component, so it adds no serving overhead. It can fail to generalize: results depend on rule delivery format, compaction strategy, and budget, and its central finding is that retaining a rule in the summary does not guarantee compliance, so a passing score on one configuration does not transfer to others. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Specification-Driven Governance for Fairness-by-Design in Agentic Software Engineering: How Far Can We Go?
item.description: This approach replaces informal or omitted fairness requirements in agentic ML development with explicit, machine-readable fairness specifications that are propagated into agent-generated artifacts. It introduces costs in the form of increased specification effort, additional governance complexity, and reliance on agent compliance without guaranteeing changes to model training or outcomes. It can fail because agents may implement fairness only as post-hoc audits, leaving models with no significant fairness improvement and no enforcement when requirements are unmet. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
item.description: This approach replaces complex multi-stage training pipelines involving mid-training, DPO, and distillation with a three-stage recipe of two SFT phases followed by RL. The cost involves implementing scalable data construction pipelines, verification systems, and RL infrastructure, which exceeds a single 24GB GPU budget for foundation model training. Adoption fails if the base model is not suitable or if the reader lacks the data engineering resources to replicate the model-aware synthesis and verification processes. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
item.description: The method replaces ad-hoc prompt engineering and manual workflow scripting with an automated pipeline that converts software documentation into executable skills and queryable references. It costs implementation effort for execution environments and trajectory logging, plus ongoing compute for validation cycles, while adding architectural complexity through persistent skill libraries and feedback loops. Version mismatches between documentation and deployed software can generate invalid skills, while insufficient validation cycles may allow overfitting to specific task instances; evolution cycles require multiple environment executions, increasing operational costs. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL
item.description: Replaces token-level supervised fine-tuning of open-weight LLMs for text-to-SQL with a constraint-aware set-contrastive objective at syntactic, semantic, and logical levels, supervised by LLM agents and verified by SQL parsing and execution on counterexample databases. Cost is a substantially more complex training pipeline (agent-proposed supervision, parser verification, counterexample database construction) plus reliance on the accompanying refined dataset, while single-pass inference remains cheap and fits one 24 GB GPU at the demonstrated 1.7B scale. It can fail when the verifier or counterexample databases do not capture schema-specific constraints, when agent-proposed supervision is noisy, and on databases or dialects far from the Spider/BIRD training distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
item.description: The framework replaces ad hoc or absent dataset-readiness assessment with a metadata-first checklist and an agentic workflow that scores datasets on FAIR/AI-FAIR criteria and returns actionable feedback for ecology and biodiversity data. Adoption costs metadata curation effort, checklist adaptation to one's domain, and LLM API or compute spend for the evaluation agent, with no model-training requirement. It can fail through evaluator hallucination or inconsistent scoring, incomplete source metadata that makes scores unactionable, and the absence of a return channel that prevents derived annotations from actually reaching data collectors. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
item.description: The SIMPLE law replaces per-model empirical fitting with a closed-form analytical model to predict inference energy from architectural hyperparameters. It costs engineering effort to implement the formula and integrate it into capacity planning or scheduling systems, rather than requiring runtime calibration per LLM. The model can fail when applied to hardware or architectures outside its validated set (13 dense LLMs on H100) or when workload characteristics deviate from the traces used for validation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
item.description: FLAMIA replaces standard high-precision attention kernels (e.g., FlashAttention in FP16/BF16) with fused low-precision MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 attention kernels purpose-built for NVIDIA Blackwell, including causal-leakage safeguards and packed variable-length document support. It requires Blackwell-generation hardware (B200/B300), custom kernel integration, and careful numeric validation; the gain materializes only on long-context causal packed-document training workloads. Failure modes include numerical divergence in low-precision pretraining if scaling or forward/backward consistency is mishandled, no benefit on non-Blackwell hardware, and limited applicability to inference or short-context workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
item.description: The method replaces direct application of image-style partitioning-and-aggregation poisoning certificates to graphs, augmenting partitions with pseudo-labels and synthetic edges so certification works under label and structure sparsity. It costs the overhead of semi-supervised self-training plus training and aggregating many partition classifiers, which multiplies compute relative to a single GNN. It can fail when pseudo-labels are noisy or synthetic edges distort the graph distribution, and its guarantees hold only within the certified perturbation budgets evaluated. 2 independent implementations, 2102 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
item.description: Replaces aggregate harmful-action rates in safety evaluations with a framework that separates a model's stated preference (logit view) from its executed behavior (sampling view), factoring harmful-action probability into preference-to-behavior carryover and refusal-versus-unresolved outcomes. Costs are low: forced-choice prompts, logit reads, and LM-judge classification are feasible via API calls or a single GPU, but adopting it adds evaluation engineering and judge-model dependencies rather than any runtime overhead. It can fail because the method is descriptive, not preventive; it characterizes harmful tendencies without mitigating them, judge-model classifications can be unreliable, and elicitation-protocol choices (fictional framing, tool use, observability) materially change measured rates, limiting comparability. 0 independent implementations, 2102 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Low-Rank Clebsch--Gordan Coupling for Equivariant Spherical Forecasting
item.description: LCG-SFNO replaces the discretized pointwise nonlinearities of spherical Fourier neural operators, which break SO(3) equivariance through aliasing, with low-rank Clebsch-Gordan tensor-product interactions confined to a controlled low-degree band plus an exactly projected quadratic nonlinearity, implemented via a custom sparse GPU kernel (SSHCG). The cost is a specialized CUDA implementation, roughly 10 percent additional training-step time, and restriction of coupling to a low-degree band that may truncate interactions a full-bandwidth model would capture. It can fail on tasks where cross-band spectral interactions matter, on non-spherical problems where the method does not apply, and operationally if the custom kernel is not maintained against the reader's software stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
item.description: DeliverBench replaces single-task agent evaluations with end-to-end professional project benchmarks spanning 11 realistic multi-stage workflows reconstructed from domain materials. It requires expert rubric scoring across 150 chained subtasks with 2-15 rounds of feedback, imposing significant evaluation cost and complexity. Failures emerge when agents cannot maintain coherence across evolving project states, particularly in preserving traceability and propagating context through sequential dependencies. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design
item.description: The method replaces classical belief-state tracking or unstructured history compression with a quantized codebook of representative memory states designed via the RECAP objective. It requires solving a quantization problem to construct the codebook, which introduces computational overhead during design but aims to reduce the memory footprint compared to maintaining full belief states. The approach can fail if the finite memory cannot distinguish belief states identified as decision witnesses, leading to unavoidable loss as characterized by the information-theoretic converse bound. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
item.description: IdeaTaste replaces informal or anecdotal judgments of LLM research taste with a benchmark that scores proposals written from a 2025 literature snapshot against what communities actually published in 2026. Using it costs only evaluation compute and access to its data pipeline, but it is a measurement tool, not a method that improves any production system. Its findings can fail to transfer because the 18% idea-matching and 26% citation-matching scores reflect proposal generation, not downstream task performance, and the benchmark evaluates a moving target as publication cycles update. 3 independent implementations, 2226 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis
item.description: It replaces a broad, general-purpose agent harness with a minimal, auditable set of tools, guardrails, memory policies, and loop components fitted to one self-hostable model. The cost is a dataset-dependent optimization process and ongoing validation of each admitted component, rather than a universal drop-in runtime. It can fail if the expert-validated dataset is narrow or unrepresentative, if the fitted harness overfits the evaluation set, or if accuracy does not transfer across models, tasks, or deployment environments. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
item.description: RASP replaces per-task LoRA branch expansion and symmetric sparse MoE gating with a single fixed-size LoRA in which inference reads all rank-1 atoms at full rank while a cosine router restricts gradients to a top-q sparse subset, stabilized by a Gram-coherence penalty and a geometric consolidation index. The cost is additional routing and consolidation bookkeeping in the backward pass, task-boundary anchor locking logic, and implementation complexity well beyond a standard LoRA fine-tune. It can fail when tasks do not share a compatible low-rank feature space, when router channel selection misaligns with new-task inputs, and the reported gains are confined to ViT image-classification benchmarks rather than generative or language workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
item.description: DistDebug-Bench replaces ad hoc or small-scale evaluations of LLM debugging agents with a curated benchmark of 120 real distributed-system bugs across 11 systems, 5 languages, and 10 failure patterns. It costs nothing to deploy but does not itself provide a production technique; adopting its findings means adding explicit reasoning structure and consistent tool-use scoping to existing debugging agents, which adds engineering complexity without guaranteed gains. Its conclusions may not transfer to the reader's specific stack, and the identified gaps could narrow as models and agents improve, reducing the benchmark's prescriptive value. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
item.description: LoL replaces the fixed sequential execution of transformer layers with a router that dynamically orders a shared library of blocks at inference, unifying dense, depth-recurrent, and MoE-style compute allocation in one architecture. It costs a full custom pretraining run (infeasible on a single 24 GB GPU or API budget), added router complexity at inference, and it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints or accessed through third-party APIs. Routing can be unstable or uninterpretable in practice, gains over baselines are stated as merely competitive rather than superior, and the claimed controllability benefits rest on synthetic tasks that may not transfer to production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 2109 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: An Agentic Framework for Automated Power System Studies and Grid Connection Assessment
item.description: This replaces manual regulatory lookup and network study execution by engineers with an agentic system that retrieves cited evidence from a domain ontology and invokes established solvers through a tool framework. It costs the complexity of maintaining a domain-specific ontology, integrating power-system solvers, and validating agent tool-call traces, and it depends on third-party APIs and domain tooling that may not transfer outside grid connection work. It can fail through incorrect ontology retrieval, incomplete regulatory coverage as rules evolve, or solver misconfiguration, and the claimed gains apply to power-system engineering tasks, not general ML workloads. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
item.description: The method replaces manual requirements engineering and post-training recipe design with a semi-automated agent pipeline, inserting human checkpoints to validate discovered criteria before execution. It costs additional infrastructure complexity for the agent harness, human review hours for requirement validation, and implementation overhead for explicit experiment-environment specifications. After adoption, unreliable execution can still cause three-quarters of delivery attempts to fail acceptance criteria, while incomplete discovery may omit or misrepresent critical constraints such as hardware budgets and data permissions. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
item.description: This work replaces informal security assumptions about MCP tool integrations with a reproducible cross-framework measurement harness (mcpvenom) that quantifies real tool execution vulnerability. It costs engineering time to integrate the scanner and interpret results, and it introduces no runtime overhead to production inference. It can fail if teams treat the 7.2% false-positive regex scanner as sufficient defense, or if they assume framework-level mitigations exist when none were intentionally implemented. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
item.description: BISECT replaces null-space-projected (subspace-isolated) LoRA updates in exemplar-free continual learning by splitting a fixed rank-r budget into an invariant carrier from dominant joint Gram-matrix modes and a whitened novelty complement, then folding both into the frozen backbone via a closed-form precision gate. It costs nothing at inference (no extra parameters or FLOPs) and fits a single 24 GB GPU, but adds training-time complexity: Gram-matrix estimation, generalized Rayleigh whitening, and per-task spectral decomposition. It can fail if the spectral-starvation diagnosis does not transfer to the reader's domain, if the rank partition between invariant and novelty blocks is mismatched to task similarity, or if Gram statistics are noisy with small per-task data, and it addresses class-incremental vision settings rather than general LLM fine-tuning. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
item.description: The framework replaces reliance on task-pass metrics and generic safety evals by programmatically verifying both benign task completion and the absence of specified harmful side effects in shell-enabled coding agents. Adopting it costs benchmark construction and test-synthesis effort plus additional evaluation runs, and it adds harness complexity rather than improving model capability. It can fail through imperfect perturbations, incomplete or mis-specified harm tests, environment non-determinism, and false assurance from passing only the enumerated harms. 0 independent implementations, 2102 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
item.description: The method replaces manual, per-study federation formation (site selection, contract and adapter authoring, task-code preparation) with bounded LLM agents whose artifacts the runtime accepts only after digest-tied checks. It costs an agent orchestration layer, repeated verification passes, and LLM inference for every new target, and adds no benefit once sites and artifacts are fixed because conventional federated training then proceeds without the agents. It can fail through false-positive site admission (19 development failures are analyzed, and discovery precision is only 0.65), incorrect runtime-generated contracts, and dependence on site-private mappings that cannot be validated cross-site. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
item.description: The paper replaces single-turn, single-agent honesty benchmarks that explicitly pressure models to deceive with an emergent multi-agent game (Four Bridges on the Kradle platform) in which deception arises without instruction. Adoption costs are modest: the game is a prompt-based evaluation runnable through third-party APIs or a small open-weight model, but the mitigation techniques (steering vectors, adversarial honesty training) require open-weight access and additional training infrastructure. It can fail as a decision tool because results are specific to one game design, sample sizes per model may be limited, and steering or training gains on this testbed may not transfer to production deception behaviors. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
item.description: The method replaces fixed rule-based closed-loop insulin dosing (e.g., OpenAPS) with an LLM agent that reasons hourly over meals, exercise, and glucose history, adapting to individual patients; costs include per-hour frontier-API calls for a latency-tolerant but safety-critical decision loop, plus dependence on the DiabetSim simulator for all validation. Failure modes are severe: LLM dosing errors in a physiological control loop, unvalidated transfer from simulator to real patients, hallucinated inferences from sensor noise, and regulatory and clinical-liability barriers that block production deployment. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
item.description: WebHarbor replaces live-website evaluation and low-fidelity synthetic environments with 153 dockerized, deterministic reconstructions of real web services covering 3,518 tasks including authenticated workflows. The cost is substantial environment-construction effort via human-agent collaboration and the infrastructure to run many containerized sites, plus RL training that, while feasible at 4B scale, still demands GPU-hours beyond a minimal budget. What can fail is a fidelity gap between replicas and live sites (agents may overfit to simplified or outdated reproductions) and continued divergence as real services evolve. 0 independent implementations, 165 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
item.description: The method replaces pure LLM/CoT logical reasoning with a pipeline where the LLM parses natural-language constraints into structured tool calls that build an exact cover instance, and a deterministic symbolic solver computes the solution with feedback-driven refinement of the encoding. It costs orchestration complexity, an extra solver dependency, and iterative LLM calls for repair, all feasible on a single GPU or via API since no model training is required. It can fail when the LLM mis-parses constraints into invalid or under/overconstrained encodings that the feedback loop cannot repair, and the approach is validated only on Zebra-style puzzles whose uniqueness property the refinement loop exploits. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations
item.description: Replaces black-box Bayesian optimization with an LLM agent that proposes parameter trials using informal domain priors such as documentation and heuristic guides. Costs are LLM inference plus prompt/workflow engineering, with the abstract claiming reduced CPU cost but providing no quantified factor; the setup targets expensive scientific simulators, not ML serving workloads. It can fail through unvalidated LLM sampling choices, sensitivity to the quality of supplied priors, and poor transfer to objective functions or constraints that differ from cosmological calibration. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
item.description: It replaces ad hoc or translated English-centric fairness benchmarks with a preregistered, paired counterfactual protocol localized to a society's actual constituencies, instantiated for Iraq and usable with API-only model access. It costs authoring and human-review effort to build the item bank, plus statistical rigor constraints; no compute-heavy infrastructure is needed, but no evaluated-model results exist yet. It can fail through item-bank defects the pilot itself exposed: criteria leaking into prompts, token swaps breaking Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, and dialect gaps miscounted as coverage. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
item.description: The method replaces heuristic token-selection or eviction KV-cache compression with selection of interpolation nodes in the attention kernel's Hilbert space, using GEIM/Q-DEIM with linear-time surrogates (Taylor series, Performer, Random Fourier Features) and streaming updates. Exact node selection costs O(n²) in context length, so practical use requires the surrogate approximations, which add implementation complexity and approximation error; only preliminary LongBench-E results are reported, with performance described as comparable to state of the art rather than superior. Adoption can fail because the surrogate approximations may not preserve the interpolation quality at long contexts, the method is validated mainly on synthetic residual convergence plus preliminary benchmark results, and no mature open-source implementation or production latency measurements are established. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
item.description: The method replaces retraining-based or data-modification-based memorisation mitigation with a one-time identification and zeroing of task-redundant attention heads before inference. It costs an offline redundancy-identification pass over a benchmark and adds no runtime memory or latency overhead, since zeroed heads can be fused or skipped, though the paper evaluates only perplexity as the quality proxy. It can fail when memorisation is distributed across heads not flagged as redundant, when the identification benchmark mismatches the production workload, or when tasks depend on the pruned heads despite aggregate perplexity appearing stable. 1 independent implementation, 128 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Communication-Efficient Private Federated Reinforcement Learning with Post-Quantum Authentication for Vehicular Networks
item.description: The method replaces independent one-bit local differential privacy quantization with correlated shared-randomness quantization between paired vehicles to reduce aggregation error while maintaining marginal privacy. It requires paired vehicles with shared randomness, adds post-quantum authentication overhead, and increases attack accuracy from 22% to 30% at privacy budget 0.3. Pairing correlations can leak information if side information about the pairing or shared randomness is compromised. 2 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
item.description: The method replaces analytical or fully-compliant-driver simulation of ride-hailing rebalancing policies with a simulation of self-interested LLM driver agents reacting to disclosed platform rules. It costs the engineering effort of building a multi-agent simulation environment plus per-run API inference for each driver agent, and it introduces dependence on the chosen LLM's interpretation fidelity. What can fail is ecological validity: LLM agents may not reproduce real driver behavior, the two tested models may not generalize to other LLMs, and the simulation results are specific to the modeled zones and policies. 2 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ARK: Avoiding Routing Collisions for KV Cache Transfer in Disaggregated LLM Inference
item.description: ARK replaces stateless ECMP hashing of KV-cache transfers between disaggregated prefill and decode GPU pools with a distributed coordination scheme in which senders choose source ports whose hashes map concurrent long-lived flows onto distinct spine links, requiring no switch modifications or receiver-side packet reordering. The cost is the added sender-side coordination protocol and its implementation within the transfer layer, which must be deployed across the serving cluster rather than within a single inference node. It can fail or yield little benefit at small scale, since the gains depend on multi-node disaggregated deployments with RDMA fabrics where hash collisions among mega-flows actually occur; on a single-GPU setup there is no prefill/decode disaggregation and no transfer bottleneck to address. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces aggregate speculative-decoding metrics and fixed full-turn draft supervision with trajectory-conditioned training that allocates prediction budget based on prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Costs include training on intermediate assistant turns, maintaining state-conditioned estimators, and instrumenting fixed-prefix replay evaluation. Can fail if workload phases or trajectory conditions differ from the browsing and software-engineering traces used for validation, making the adaptive allocation miscalibrated. 2 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
item.description: The benchmark replaces aggregate scalar scoring of image edits with pre-generated atomic checklists that localize failures, and the harness replaces ad hoc fine-tuning with a multi-agent loop of failure diagnosis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation. Adoption costs the engineering effort of building checklists and running iterative diagnose-generate-finetune-reevaluate cycles, plus GPU or API budget for data generation and supervised adaptation on a 24 GB card. Gains are demonstrated only on the authors' selected Top-5 failure targets and may not transfer to a user's actual production distribution; the improvement loop also depends on the checklist quality and can overfit to the benchmark's own decomposition. 1 independent implementation, 128 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RTL-Interact: Training EDA-Interactive Models for Multi-Task RTL Design
item.description: The method replaces separate RTL generation and repair components with a single model post-trained to generate RTL, construct EDA checks, and revise from tool feedback. It costs multi-task demonstration construction, staged supervision, and reinforcement learning against EDA tools, which exceeds a 24 GB GPU budget and requires licenses and infrastructure for commercial EDA flows. It can fail if EDA tool access is limited, if reward gating biases toward concise but weak checks, or if gains on CVDP, VerilogEval v2, and RTLLM v2 do not transfer to proprietary design styles and constraints. 1 independent implementation, 128 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MEMIG: Self-evolving Memory Construction for Antibody Optimization
item.description: Replaces free-form natural-language memory (maintained by rewriting) with indexable, quantitative, structured records keyed by domain-grounded identifiers, with interactions measured via epistasis decomposition of evaluated sets. Costs include implementing the identifier scheme and decomposition machinery, maintaining oracle-backed updates, and restricting memory to domains with measurable properties rather than general narratable experience. Can fail if the property oracle is noisy, expensive, or unavailable, if interventions are misidentified or the epistasis decomposition misattributes interactions, or if exact-lookup structure becomes brittle outside antibody-style optimization. 1 independent implementation, 128 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: ASTC replaces external trained context compressors and hard-token rewriting by using the model's own GDN recurrent state to carry absorbed context as soft tokens alongside exact hard tokens, reducing later-layer attention computation and yielding reusable KV caches. It is training-free, but it requires a hybrid Gated Delta Network-attention architecture and direct control of the forward pass, so it cannot be applied to standard transformer checkpoints or third-party inference APIs. It can fail if the soft-token state omits decision-relevant evidence in tasks where the recurrent summary drifts from the details later needed, and gains depend on the agent trajectory producing compressible context. 2 independent implementations, 18 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Migrating a Legacy Scientific Application with an AI Coding Agent: NICAM from Fortran to Kokkos
item.description: The technique replaces manual Fortran-to-C++/Kokkos porting of a large legacy scientific application with direct translation by an AI coding agent (Claude Code) under human review, converting roughly 140,000 lines of Fortran into 35,000 lines of C++/Kokkos. Costs include sustained human expert review, ensemble-based statistical validation (a 100-member comparison against the original model), and porting effort across the dynamical core and seven physics packages. What can fail: subtle numerical or behavioral divergence from the original model that statistical ensemble checks may miss, and performance portability is not guaranteed—the HIP build on MI300A only reached parity after bandwidth normalization, so gains depend on target hardware and kernel characteristics. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning
item.description: Replaces the implicit fallback behavior in training-free MoE expert pruning: what the layer computes when a router selects a pruned expert, comparing rerouting, constant mean-output replacement (MoNE), partial expert copies, and a proposed closed-form low-rank map ('tilted novice'). Cost is low: the tilted novice adds only 1.2-1.8% parameters at 50% pruning, is training-free, and is stable under 3- and 4-bit quantization; no operator dominates, so per-model validation is required. Failure modes are significant: results flip depending on whether the router was trained with top-k renormalization, the calibration domain shifts the pruning mask 4-9x more than resampling, and 25% pruning can retain 92-97% of multiple-choice accuracy while collapsing to 0-17% of code and 5-65% of GSM8K scores. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
item.description: Ask on Demand replaces pre-emptive sharing and summarization with a pull-based mechanism where agents query peers for specific evidence only when needed. It requires training a lightweight gate using paired team continuations and final outcome labels, which adds pipeline complexity and implementation overhead beyond standard API-based agent frameworks. The gate can fail to approve necessary queries or approve wasteful ones, and the approach depends on maintaining accessible peer execution histories at inference time. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cross-Interface Authorization for AI Computer-Use Agents
item.description: This method replaces ad-hoc, per-interface permission checks with a unified, commit-time verification protocol that normalizes requests across disparate execution routes into canonical effects. It costs significant engineering complexity to implement the profile-bounded specification and adds computational overhead for runtime verification, ticket issuance, and state re-validation at commit. Failures occur if the route inventory is incomplete (allowing bypass via unenumerated paths), if the authoritative state changes between prepare and commit phases, or if the underlying infrastructure lacks a unified policy decision point capable of intercepting all effect-bearing routes. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Safety Checks Become Privacy Risks: A Privacy-Preserving Paradigm for LLM Agent Safety Auditing
item.description: The method replaces plaintext outsourcing of pre-execution tool-call audits with a three-domain pipeline using trusted representation construction, CKKS-encrypted similarity scoring, and execution bound to audited calls. It adds encrypted-computation infrastructure, learned audit representations, and explicit interfaces, with reported online scoring latency of 0.176 s per operation plus offline setup and key-management overhead. It can fail if representation quality drops on unseen tools or domains, if the semi-honest auditor and trust-boundary assumptions do not match the deployment, or if the binary audit misses multi-step and context-dependent unsafe behavior. 0 independent implementations, 2093 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
item.description: SACQ replaces standard LLM-inherited post-training weight quantization (e.g., uniform GPTQ-style recipes) for Vision-Language-Action models with structure-aware vector-codebook fitting, action-error-driven mixed-bit allocation, and a two-stage codeword and scale refinement calibrated against decoded actions. The cost is a multi-stage quantization pipeline requiring calibration data, per-layer sensitivity measurement through the action head, and reimplementation of codebook fitting rather than an off-the-shelf PTQ call; activation quantization and low-precision attention add further engineering. It can fail when the target model or task distribution differs from GR00T N1.7 and LIBERO/SimplER, since codebooks and bit allocations are fitted to specific input statistics and downstream action sensitivity, and results do not generalize to non-VLA LLM workloads. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
item.description: It replaces screenshot-only mouse-and-keyboard computer use with a unified interface combining code/CLI tools, accessibility-tree actions, and GUI control, supported by compact AX observations, batched actions, AX diffs, and stale-state guards. The cost is added interface and orchestration complexity: the agent must maintain channel-specific tooling, synchronize state across programmatic, semantic, and visual views, and follow a skill policy for choosing channels safely. It can fail when AX state is incomplete or stale, when channel switching produces inconsistent observations, or when a model selects the wrong channel for an app and accumulates execution errors despite stronger benchmark results. 1 independent implementation, 17 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What Does a Repair Agent Gain from Remembering Its Failure? An Exploratory Study on Real Python Bugs
item.description: The technique replaces blind retry of a failed repair agent with a retry conditioned on failure memory such as the prior transcript or extracted test signals. It costs roughly one extra failed attempt's context tokens per retry, and a model-written lesson adds a further model call with no measured benefit over the raw transcript. Adoption can fail because gains were not statistically significant, outcomes varied more across bugs than across conditions, and retries shown prior test results more often broke other tests, inflating apparent gains on the bug-revealing test. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $ε$-close Surrogates
item.description: The method replaces direct low-rank matrix completion with an over-parameterized formulation whose observation-mask nullspace is perturbed with epsilon-level noise, yielding epsilon-close surrogates with valid RIP constants. Its cost is primarily mathematical and implementation complexity, with no stated reduction in production latency, memory, or API spend, and no benchmark evidence for LLM workloads. It can fail in practice if the assumed entry-wise independent observation model or perturbation regime does not hold, and the guarantees do not translate directly to production inference systems. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
item.description: The technique replaces direct fine-tuning or full model switching by patching key-value (KV) cache states from a fine-tuned model into a base model (or vice versa) to transfer specific behaviors like language switching or misalignment. It costs inference-time computation for cache manipulation and adds complexity in identifying pivotal token positions, with no training required but potential latency overhead during cache swapping. Failures include inconsistent behavior transfer if patched positions are not pivotal, reliance on attention mechanisms that may not generalize across prompts, and inability to fully replicate or remove fine-tuned behaviors in all cases. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sparse Text Diffusion under Dual Budgets: Context Connectivity and Expert Activation
item.description: The technique replaces dense token interaction and feed-forward computation in long-context text diffusion with two explicit budgets: a sparse attention graph and conditional expert activation. The reported cost is a 20% reduction relative to DiffuSeq, but this comes with the complexity of managing separate graph and expert budgets and the risk that sparsity alone does not preserve document-level information. Potential failure modes include degradation on tasks requiring global coherence, as the analysis notes mixed ablation results and separates measured observations from unverified claims about training speed and memory. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HiState: Hierarchical Prefix Cache Management for Hybrid LLM Serving in Agentic Workloads
item.description: HiState replaces the prefix-cache policies in hybrid-model serving stacks such as vLLM-Marconi and SGLang-HiCache, which retain recurrent checkpoints only at selected boundaries and therefore miss or recompute reusable prefixes in agent workloads. It adds SSD-tiered checkpoint storage, adaptive checkpoint-interval control, and unified eviction, which increases storage-management complexity and requires SSD capacity; the recurrent-checkpoint read is bounded per hit, but the KV path still depends on fast memory. It can fail when the serving stack or model is not a supported hybrid architecture, when SSD latency or capacity is misconfigured, or when the workload lacks the agentic prefix-reuse patterns that justify the extra hierarchy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ORION: An Outcome-Driven LLM Advisor for RL-Based Multi-Domain 6G Slice Placement
item.description: The method replaces a memoryless LLM placement planner (or FIFO episodic store) with an outcome-driven episodic memory that records network-condition profiles, proposed plans, and verified feasibility outcomes, feeding labelled successes and failures back to the planner. It costs memory infrastructure to store and retrieve episode records, plus a feasibility-verification step per completed attempt, and it presumes a downstream multi-agent RL coordinator that treats plans as soft priors. It can fail when deployment conditions drift from recorded profiles, when importance-based retention discards rare but critical failure modes, or when the domain-specific RL execution layer cannot be reproduced, since the gain was demonstrated only within a simulated 6G slice-placement environment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B: Adapting a 2.6B Hybrid Model to Tajik Tool Calling, and What Continued Pretraining Takes Away
item.description: The method replaces reliance on the base model's native tool-calling ability for Tajik with a two-stage recipe: LoRA continued pretraining on 1.49M Tajik documents followed by SFT on a mixed tool-call corpus with English replay. It costs continued-pretraining compute on top of SFT, erases the native tool-call format (every CPT checkpoint scores zero), and regresses English MMLU from 60.8 to 52.5. After adoption it can fail by almost never declining when no tool fits (6.9% correct), weak multi-turn calling, and calls that require verification before execution. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Understanding the Energy Cost of Quantized Agents on Shared GPUs
item.description: This joint precision-and-admission framework replaces default 8-bit weight-activation quantization or un-tuned 4-bit weight quantization for agent workloads. It requires empirical validation of cache admission limits per model to prevent the 49% energy-per-completion penalty observed in live runs. When agents compete for constrained cache (e.g., 40 GB deployments), high admission rates with 4-bit weights increase energy per verified completion by 34%. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
item.description: It replaces direct CoT extraction and manual rationale writing by generating answer-conditioned synthetic reasoning traces for SFT. Cost is inference spend and engineering for generation, cleaning, filtering, and validation, with added dataset-governance overhead. It can fail through rationale hallucination, answer-rationalization rather than faithful reasoning, benchmark leakage, and terms-of-use or policy constraints on model-generated training data. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
item.description: It replaces training-free, layer-wise-reconstruction VQ quantization (e.g., GPTQ-style codebook fitting) with gradient-based optimization of quantized weights via straight-through estimation and block-wise distillation. The cost is a training phase with calibration data, optimizer memory overhead during training, and a more complex implementation than one-shot PTQ, though inference cost is unchanged. It can fail if the block-wise distillation schedule or hyperparameters do not transfer to the reader's model, if calibration data mismatches production distribution, or if downstream inference stacks do not support the chosen VQ scheme's codebook format. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn
item.description: The method replaces uniform or Fisher-mass-based KV-cache quantization with a per-cell error allocation derived from a diagnostic of where keys versus values dominate KL in looped language models (Ouro, Huginn). It costs an offline Fisher/KL diagnostic pass and per-model allocation computation, with measured KL savings at 25-48% of BF16 bytes, but no demonstrated latency or serving throughput gain since quantization is simulated. It can fail because the local second-order prediction misses confident outlier rows, the shared-weight error factor at 32 loops is direction-dependent (1.65-4.09), the measured-cost allocator's edge over Fisher does not transfer to Ouro-2.6B, and 60 of 176 registered criteria failed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
item.description: SimXAI replaces the GUS-style pipeline (intent recognition, dialogue management, template-based generation) of conversational XAI agents with a single tool-calling LLM that routes to existing XAI resources. It costs LLM inference (API or a small local model on the 24 GB GPU) plus implementation of tool schemas for the underlying XAI methods, and removes the modular GUS components. It can fail through incorrect tool selection on ambiguous or context-dependent queries, unfaithful responses if the LLM deviates from tool outputs, and dependence on the availability and correctness of the external XAI resources it calls. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents
item.description: This technique replaces a static video director agent with a self-evolving system comprising a director, a simulated user, and a meta-engineer. It requires maintaining and coordinating three separate LLM agents in a feedback loop, which increases architectural complexity and inference costs compared to single-agent approaches. The simulated user may fail to accurately represent diverse real-world user intents and interaction patterns, limiting the system's adaptability in production. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
item.description: This is not a deployable technique but an attack study: it shows that MCP tool-call traces, even without conversation content, leak user attributes and can substitute for direct access to user data on the attacker's side. For the reader, the cost of the implied mitigation is operational: minimizing logged tool arguments and results, isolating sessions, and restricting trace retention adds engineering complexity and can reduce observability and debugging capability. The main failure mode is assuming conversation-level redaction suffices while tool arguments, returned results, and cross-session linkage continue to expose behavioral signals. 1 independent implementation, 2093 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Binary Sparse Codes: Where are we on Energy Efficient Representations?
item.description: The paper proposes an evaluation framework that measures information preservation as similarity preservation for binary sparse codes, intended to replace ad-hoc or absent quantitative comparisons of sparse coding methods; it does not introduce a new production inference method to replace an existing component in an LLM stack. Applying the framework costs implementation and benchmarking effort across multiple coding models, and adopting binary sparse representations can impose additional encoding/decoding complexity and potential accuracy loss relative to dense representations. The reported trade-off can fail to yield a practical benefit in deployment if the achievable sparsity does not translate into end-to-end latency or energy gains on the available 24 GB GPU or API-based pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
item.description: Replaces DPO-based prompt-injection defense training (e.g., Meta-SecAlign) with the SecPO loss anchored on an approximated injection-invariant reference model plus an adversarial training pipeline that synthesizes strong best@240 injections. Costs are a full adversarial fine-tuning run with attack synthesis (240-step optimization per sample) on a 27B model, which likely exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without third-party training APIs, though the released model and training data are freely usable. Can fail against novel adaptive attacks outside the training distribution, and reported gains are validated mainly on the authors' attack suite and AgentDojo benchmark. 0 independent implementations, 2093 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces static prompting and memory-only negotiation agents with an agent that consolidates prior experience, models opponents, and adapts strategy across episodes using execution-grounded settlement outcomes, without updating base LLM weights. The cost is a purpose-built simulation environment (TradeWar) with capacity and network constraints, multi-episode orchestration, and iterative strategy refinement infrastructure, all of which require substantial domain-specific engineering beyond standard LLM deployment. It can fail if the settlement model does not reflect real-world trade dynamics, if cross-episode adaptation overfits to simulation artifacts, or if the Economic Health Index misaligns with actual production objectives, and the approach has not been validated outside this benchmark. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness
item.description: CRoS replaces outcome-only RLVR rewards and perturbation-based causality rewards with a causality metric that scrambles the order of reasoning steps without altering step content, rewarding CoTs that causally drive the final answer. The cost is substantial: it requires running reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on a reasoning model, including generating multiple CoT rollouts, scrambling steps, and re-querying the model to measure answer changes, all of which multiply compute per training step well beyond standard fine-tuning. Failure modes include reward hacking where the model learns to produce CoTs that merely appear order-sensitive, degraded performance on tasks where step order is naturally flexible, and the confound that some valid reasoning is genuinely order-invariant, in which case the metric penalizes correct behavior. 1 independent implementation, 124 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
item.description: ZHA replaces quadratic full attention (and sparsity methods whose indexers scale quadratically) with a hierarchical tree of compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which queries traverse top-down to retrieve a sparse key subset. Cost: the tree must be built and maintained over the KV cache, adding memory and implementation complexity, and adapting an existing pretrained model requires a KL distillation stage over a few billion tokens plus custom traversal kernels to realize the theoretical gains. What can fail: the benefit only materializes beyond roughly 1M context where the reader's single 24 GB GPU cannot operate anyway; routing errors from compressed summaries can degrade retrieval and reasoning quality; and there is no mature open-source implementation or hardware-efficient kernel yet, so realized speedups may fall far short of the performance model. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
item.description: The technique replaces manual hand-coding of agent harnesses and policy finetuning by using a coding model to iteratively diagnose rollout failures and revise control code around frozen policies. It requires a coding model capable of interpreting robotics trajectories, a simulation or physical setup for rollouts, and held-out evaluation scenes to prevent overfitting. Post-adoption risks include harnesses overfitting to specific optimization episodes, failure to generalize to out-of-distribution tasks, and the need for robotics infrastructure unavailable to teams without existing manipulation hardware. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
item.description: Flide replaces generation-oriented serving stacks (vLLM/SGLang) that recompute shared prefixes or distort probabilities when executing branching decision-model queries, instead flattening the logical request tree into one token stream with GPU-resident fork metadata and checkpointed agent histories. It requires adopting a custom inference engine with ForkAttention over both standard attention and Gated DeltaNet layers, plus pre-recorded execution graphs, which adds integration and maintenance cost beyond commodity serving frameworks. It can fail if the workload is not dominated by branching categorical decision queries, if the specific decision/hybrid models (e.g., Jev-style or Gated DeltaNet architectures) are not the ones deployed, or if the unreleased/immature implementation cannot be operated on a single 24 GB GPU within a small team's budget. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Intrinsic Information Rates of Summaries in Simulation-Based Inference
item.description: The method replaces deterministic fixed-dimensional summary encoders in simulation-based inference with stochastic binary bottlenecks whose mutual-information rate is measured and matched across candidates. The cost is added encoder and training complexity, the need to estimate each trained summary's information rate, and potential sampling variance during posterior estimation. It can fail if the simulator violates the common-support condition, if rate estimation is inaccurate at the target budget, or if the benchmark-specific ranking reverses at the information budget used in production. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MCF: A Memory- and Communication-Aware Co-Designed Framework for Long-Context LLM Inference
item.description: It replaces static KV-cache layouts and prefill-to-decode layout conversion with MARS, which replicates hot KV blocks during early prefill and progressively drains them into a sharded decode-ready layout while routing only lightweight queries across stationary KV shards. Its cost is an FPGA compute-NIC datapath plus a distributed, metadata-driven orchestration layer that is far beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-based stack and adds substantial systems complexity. It can fail when the assumed early-prefill memory headroom or multi-worker communication bottlenecks are absent, and its scaling advantages are unverifiable without a cluster. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
item.description: The method replaces standard all-layer LoRA, which fine-tunes every transformer layer, with LoRA applied only to task-relevant layers identified by a frozen-base zero-ablation calibration pass. It reduces adapter parameters roughly 3.5x while adding a per-task calibration step and per-task layer-selection bookkeeping; training compute per step is otherwise comparable to standard LoRA. Layer importance is reported as highly task-dependent with limited cross-task overlap, so a selection calibrated on one task or benchmark can underperform on another, and results are demonstrated on a single 1.5B model and may not transfer to other architectures, scales, or non-reasoning workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SPARTA: A Sparse Ternary LLM Accelerator with Adaptive Attention and Unified Datapath for Long-Context Edge Inference
item.description: SPARTA replaces conventional GPU/CPU edge inference and separate ternary-linear and attention datapaths with a custom unified accelerator combining ternary-weight SpMM/SpMV, bit-serial attention, and page-level Top-k plus token-level Top-p KV-cache pruning. Its gains depend on fabricating or programming dedicated hardware and on 1.58-bit ternary models, and the adaptive attention prunes KV access at the cost of task-dependent quality loss. It can fail in applicability terms: the results are accelerator-specific, quality degradation varies by task and pruning aggressiveness, and nothing here transfers directly to a 24 GB GPU or API-based stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
item.description: FlowVQ replaces the standard VQ-VAE quantizer with jointly learned EMA/codebook-update schemes by transporting fixed even-quantile prior codes through a lightweight flow-matching probability flow ODE to define the codebook. It adds training-time complexity and extra compute for learning and integrating the flow, plus sensitivity to flow-training stability, while inference tokenization cost depends on the final implementation and may remain near standard VQ lookup if the codebook is materialized. It can fail through distribution mismatch between latent encodings and the transported prior, degraded reconstruction on high-precision data, or implementation overhead that negates the claimed utilization benefit. 1 independent implementation, 107 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
item.description: Replaces full fine-tuning or reliance on base/prompt-only models for clinical QA by applying LoRA-based instruction tuning on a small expert-reviewed dataset. Cost is modest: tuning an 8B model with LoRA fits on a 24 GB GPU, but requires curated QA pairs, expert review, and evaluation infrastructure. Can fail through residual hallucination, dataset bias from only 500 QA pairs, limited external generalization, and clinical safety risks if deployed without guardrails. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
item.description: Replaces vocabulary-scale distribution transmission with a server-side replica of the draft model, exchanging only token indices and scalar probabilities. Costs include maintaining model consistency across device-server boundary, double draft model storage, and synchronization complexity. Fails if replica drift occurs or when speculative decoding itself is unsuitable for the workload. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering
item.description: The method replaces standard RAG context packing and common Lost-in-the-Middle mitigations such as reordering, reranking, or generic multi-agent reasoning with a dual-view local/global agent design plus quality-aware pruning. It costs added orchestration and inference overhead versus a single-pass RAG pipeline, though the paper claims lower cost than prior multi-agent frameworks. It can fail when relevance or quality scoring is inaccurate, when pruning removes useful evidence, or when the extra local/global passes do not repay their latency and implementation complexity on a given workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings
item.description: RRC replaces the corpus-derived spectral weighting rules used by PCA, Whitening, and SpecTemp with a closed-form, relevance-guided calibration that adjusts per-direction log weights via a fitted power-law trend plus a residual, without retraining the encoder or adding an inference stage. Its costs are the need for relevance judgments to estimate positive--negative margin weights per retained direction and an offline calibration step applied to the shared query--document transformation; runtime cost remains that of the underlying spectral compressor. It can fail if relevance judgments are scarce or biased, if the assumed margin-based weighting does not match the retrieval objective, or if the estimated residuals overfit dataset-specific relevance signals and do not transfer across encoders, domains, or quantization settings. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning
item.description: Replaces standard activation units (or supplements layers) with a differentiable predicate neuron that quantizes inputs and a choice state to perform fuzzy first-order logic operations with a hard-forward, differentiable-backward gradient mechanism. Costs an additional trainable parameter per neuron, a custom gradient implementation (available in Keras/PyTorch), and added architectural complexity without published latency or memory overhead measurements. Can fail if benchmark gains on MNIST/Wikitext do not transfer to the target workload, if the hard/soft gradient mismatch causes training instability at scale, or if maintenance of a custom module outweighs modest accuracy benefits. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Multi-Draft On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Drafters
item.description: MDraft replaces single-draft on-policy distillation of one-step diffusion drafters by sampling several draft blocks per context and aggregating verifier full-vocabulary conditionals across their prefixes into the training target. It costs additional drafter sampling and verifier forward passes during training, while drafter architecture and inference procedure remain unchanged. It can fail if the reader does not already operate a diffusion-based speculative decoding stack, since training requires verifier access for distillation and the benefit vanishes for autoregressive drafters or API-only deployments. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Selective and Hybrid-State Communication for Latent Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: The method replaces natural-language message passing between agents with selective transfer of KV caches and recurrent states through a shared workspace. It costs implementation complexity, direct access to model internals, and some quality risk, including a six-point drop on HumanEval+ for SelectKV.
